session_cue.text: "Ow, why did you do that?" - Squints

previous.text: The party caught the Clurichen Naggeneen in the Golden Egg's basement and handed him to Quinn. Quinn hung him in a bag behind his bar.
Trout recruited the newly arrived halfling Squints as a junior assistant in his Halfling Corps.
Dunk spotted a glowing magical mithril chain shirt in Warwick the smith's shop and planned to get it.
Dunk traded for faun wine at the Faun Grove and gave Ingrid a watered-down batch for her sleeping potion.
One-armed survivor George told the party where the black dragon's lair is and how it killed his companions.
Father William marked Brandon's Barrow Mound on the party's map, and the party set out for it.
The party rescued Brother Dirk from a man-eating giant's cottage and outran the giant.

current.where_you_are: The party is in the woods north of town with Squints and the rescued monk Brother Dirk. They are across the field from the giant's stone cottage, after outrunning the giant.

immediate_intention.text: The party is heading north to the Barrow and is pressing Brother Dirk to come with them. Dirk still says he should just head home, and Trout has told him he will report to Squints.

Your goals.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
Kill the black dragon and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Get the magical mithril chain shirt from Warwick the smith's shop.

Standing in your way.text: George says nothing pierces the black dragon's scales. His companions' arrows and swords all failed.

What could help.text: If Dunk helps Ingrid give Warwick her sleeping potion tonight, he can enter the shop for the mithril shirt while the smith sleeps. The potion isn't made yet, and Dunk heavily diluted the faun wine.
Father William says that if the party retrieves the magic sword from Brandon's Barrow Mound, they can kill the black dragon. George says no one knows if the legend is true.
If the party returns to the Clumsy Fox and hires Lady Hilda, the seasoned warrior will join them against the dragon.
If the party pays Drop Dead Ned 100 gold for the week, he and his killer wasp will do anything as long as he gets to kill people. He gives back 5 gold for each permitted kill.

Still unanswered.text: What has become of the shipments to Brandonsford?
Who is Vivian the witch, and does she share a coven with Ingrid?

Promises and debts.text: Dr. Uriah must do penance at Brandon's Barrow Mound, as he promised Father William.
Dr. Uriah must donate 10 gold for the Barrow Mound's upkeep, as he promised Father William.
Dunk must help Ingrid into Warwick's house and give Warwick the sleeping potion once she has made it.
Trout and the party owe Squints second pick of the first treasure, after the elite members. Until then, Squints pays for himself and his gear.
Sir Phidipaldi must bring his lance against the dragon, as he vowed to George.

Meanwhile.text: The black dragon has a fatally poisonous bite and spits sulfur. George says it can't fly yet but soon will, and then the town is doomed.
A man-eating giant lives in a huge stone cottage on the party's route north and may seize travelers who pass.

threads.name: The unrecognized treasure map
threads.note: Uriah still knows nothing of the map's history. The party plans to check a marked location on the way to the Barrow, but the treasure is not yet found.

threads.name: The Clurichen from the riverbanks
threads.note: The question is answered: the Clurichen Naggeneen comes into town to drink Quinn's stock (beat_18). He is captured but not destroyed, hanging in a bag behind Quinn's bar with his fate unsettled (beat_22, beat_39).

threads.name: The black dragon and Eric the Reeve's bounty
threads.note: The hunt changed shape: the party learned the dragon reportedly can't be killed without Brandon's sword (beat_47), that it will soon fly, and that Eric may lack the bounty. Phidipaldi also vowed to bring his lance for George (beat_59).

threads.name: The missing shipments to Brandonsford
threads.note: Shipments still have not come in, and the cause remains unknown.

threads.name: Drop Dead Ned's offer of hire
threads.note: Not touched this Session; Ned was only seen in the tavern.

threads.name: Shamus the mule
threads.note: Dunk offered 20 gold. Gill will lower the price only once his sons come back, which changes the terms of the purchase.

threads.name: Quinn's vanishing ale and the deal against Bentley
threads.note: The thief was caught and revealed as Naggeneen rather than Bentley (beat_21). Quinn paid Phidipaldi, Trout and Uriah 33 gold each (beat_22), so nothing remains owed or unknown.

threads.name: Squints and Trout's Halfling Corps
threads.note: Trout recruited Squints on terms that include second pick of the first treasure, which is still owed (beat_42). The party secretly treats him as expendable, and Dirk now reports to him.

threads.name: Warwick's mithril chain shirt
threads.note: Dunk wants the glowing magical mithril shirt in Warwick's shop and says he has a plan to get it. He only remarked that it could help against the dragon, so it stands on its own.

threads.name: Ingrid's sleeping potion for Warwick
threads.note: Dunk proposed the potion to get himself and Ingrid into Warwick's house (beat_34, beat_35), so it serves the armor plan. He delivered diluted faun wine and the potion is not yet made, so the meeting and his help getting her in are still pending.

threads.name: Brandon's sword in the Barrow Mound
threads.note: Father William says the dragon can't be killed without this sword (beat_47), which makes it a child of the dragon hunt. The party is heading to the Barrow, and rescued Brother Dirk wants to go home instead.

threads.name: Vivian, the witch in the woods
threads.note: Father William and Ingrid describe Vivian as a witch with ties to Ingrid. Her home is now marked on the map, and the party chose to avoid it, so the question of her stands apart.

threads.name: Uriah's penance and donation for Father William
threads.note: Uriah promised to do penance at the Barrow Mound and donate 10 gold for its upkeep, and has done neither yet.

threads.name: The man-eating giant in the woods
threads.note: The party stole the giant's intended meal and outran him, but the giant still lives near the route north. Escaping did not end the danger.

facts.text: Find the treasure marked on the party's treasure map.
The party holds a treasure map whose marked locations they do not recognize; they assume the treasure is in one of those places.

classification.support_basis: The map is the party's only guide to the treasure, but its locations are unrecognized, so it narrows the search without yet pointing anywhere usable.

facts.text: Where are the places marked on the treasure map, and which holds the treasure?

classification.grounding_justification: Play explicitly states the party does not recognize the map's marked locations and the surrounding land is unknown to them.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Answering it means identifying locations, a largely factual discovery rather than a hidden circumstance.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental for finding the treasure, though mildly interesting.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Locals, landmarks and exploration of the unknown land could plausibly be used to match the map.

facts.text: The party plans to check out one of the map's marked locations on the way to the Barrow.

classification.support_basis: Visiting a marked location directly tests whether the treasure is there, though it is unknown which location holds it.
classification.action_basis: The party agreed to Trout's proposal to stop at a marked location en route to the Barrow; it is simply searching the map's locations.
classification.opening_basis: The route to the Barrow passes a marked location; checking it is direct pursuit of the treasure itself rather than an additional enabling circumstance.

facts.text: What is the history of the party's treasure map?

classification.grounding_justification: Play notes that Uriah, who carries the map, recalls nothing of its history, but nothing makes this conspicuous beyond the gap.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Its origin could reveal who made it and why, a modest underlying circumstance.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: No sources or leads about the map's origin have been established.

facts.text: Reginald the frog says a trickster creature called a Clurichen comes from the riverbanks into Brandonsford every night, up to no good, and that the party should stay away from wherever it goes.
facts.ended_how: no longer relevant: the Clurichen Naggeneen was caught and now hangs in a bag behind Quinn's bar

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: The creature is only said to be a trickster 'up to no good'; no particular harm is named.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: A trickster's mischief suggests minor harm or inconvenience; nothing serious is established.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Rests on the testimony of a single frog, Reginald, whose reliability is unestablished.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: Reginald says it comes into town every night, an ongoing pattern, though no specific harm is tied to it.
classification.preventability_justification: The party can heed the warning and avoid where it goes, but has no established means to stop it.

facts.text: What is the Clurichen doing when it comes into town each night?
facts.ended_how: answered: Naggeneen comes into town to drink Quinn's stock

classification.grounding_justification: Reginald's statement that it is 'up to no good' every night raises the question without framing it explicitly.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden nightly activity, a hidden circumstance in town.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Learning its mischief could explain events in town, but nothing yet ties it to any.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could be pursued by watching at night or following it from the riverbanks.

facts.text: What does Quinn intend to do with Naggeneen, who hangs captive in a bag behind his bar?

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn pointedly says he knows what he will do with Naggeneen without saying what, and the bag still hangs there the next morning.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer is Quinn's plan, a single fact he could simply reveal.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting as the fate of the captured spirit, but mainly a loose end.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Asking Quinn would likely settle it.

facts.text: Naggeneen offered his pot of gold or a secret in exchange for being let go; he now hangs in a bag behind Quinn's bar, and Sir Phidipaldi refused the offer.

classification.support_basis: Gold or an unnamed secret has no established connection to any want or debt of the party.
classification.action_basis: Naggeneen made the offer, but he is now Quinn's captive and play establishes neither access to him nor Quinn's consent to release him, nor a want the reward serves.
classification.opening_basis: Releasing the captive would earn his gold or a secret, but this adds no established advantage toward any want or debt.

facts.resource_subject: Naggeneen captive in a bag behind Quinn's bar

facts.text: Kill the black dragon near Brandonsford and drag its body into town to collect Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold.
Lady Hilda, a seasoned warrior in chain mail, offers to join the party against the dragon for pay, though she won't go alone; the party must return to the Clumsy Fox and hire her.

classification.support_basis: A more seasoned fighter than the party adds real strength against the dragon, at an unset price.
classification.action_basis: Hilda explicitly offered to join adventurers against the dragon for money.
classification.opening_basis: Hilda's actual offer of paid service adds an experienced ally to the dragon hunt, beyond merely pursuing the dragon.

facts.text: Farmer Gill says the big work he needs is killing the dragon outside town; Dunk could offer that work in trade for the mule Shamus.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon could stand in for the 100 gold price of Shamus, though Gill never explicitly agreed to such a trade.
classification.action_basis: Dunk asked to trade work for the mule and Gill answered that the big work needed is killing the dragon.
classification.opening_basis: Gill names dragon-killing as work worth trading, letting Dunk get the mule without paying 100 gold.

facts.text: George, a capable woodsman living a couple of houses from the Clumsy Fox, encountered the dragon; the party could question him about where and how he met it.
facts.ended_how: used up: Sir Phidipaldi questioned George about the dragon

classification.support_basis: An eyewitness could help the party find the dragon and know what to expect, though his cooperation is unconfirmed.
classification.action_basis: Eric named George, where he lives, and that he met the dragon; asking him is a straightforward option.
classification.opening_basis: A known eyewitness can be questioned to learn where the dragon was met, an advantage beyond simply hunting it.

facts.text: The black dragon terrorizing Brandonsford's surroundings has a fatally poisonous bite and spits sulfur; it killed George's companions and cost him his arm. George says it can't fly yet but soon will, and then the town is doomed.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Deaths and maiming of those who meet it, and once it flies, ruin of the town, are specific harms.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: George says the town will be doomed once it flies, and it has already killed several hunters.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: George is a direct survivor whose account is detailed and corroborated by his lost arm.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: George warns it is on the verge of flight, an advancing process, though no timeline is given.
classification.preventability_justification: Killing the dragon would end it, though it reportedly needs Brandon's sword.

facts.classification_change_basis: George's eyewitness account (beat_55, beat_56) adds deaths, imminent flight and a threat to the whole town, raising severity and evidentiary strength; the reported need for Brandon's sword lowers preventability.

facts.text: Farmer Gill's three sons are hunting the dragon now and could be maimed or killed as George was.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Injury or death of the sons in a fight with the dragon is identifiable.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Death or maiming of three young men would be serious.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: Their hunt is stated by Gill, but harm to them rests on inference from George's injury.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: They are actively hunting, but no encounter or warning is described.
classification.preventability_justification: The party could seek them out or kill the dragon first, but where they are is unknown.

facts.text: George says nothing pierces the black dragon's scales; his companions' arrows and swords all failed.

classification.scope_basis: The dragon's invulnerable scales are a lasting property that stands in the way of any attempt to kill it.

facts.text: Brandon's magic sword, which Father William says is needed to kill the dragon, would let the party kill it (see thread_11).

classification.support_basis: It is reportedly the only weapon that can kill the dragon, though George says the legend's truth and the sword's whereabouts are uncertain.
classification.action_basis: The party has decided to go to the Barrow where the sword is said to be buried.
classification.opening_basis: A sword with a specific alleged dragon-killing capability would overcome the dragon's invulnerability.

facts.resource_subject: Brandon's sword as the only way to kill the dragon

facts.text: George says the dragon's lair is up north at the foot of the mountains, reachable without climbing.

classification.support_basis: Knowing roughly where the lair is lets the party find the dragon, though the location is only general.

facts.text: Does Eric the Reeve actually have the 1000 gold he promised for the dragon?

classification.grounding_justification: George explicitly doubts Eric has the money, raising the question directly.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A single discovery about Eric's means would settle it.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly practical, bearing on whether the reward is real.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Could involve asking around about Eric, but little more.

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi vowed to George, in return for his account of the dragon, to bring his lance against it.

classification.stake_basis: George asked only that the dragon be killed in return; he doubts Phidipaldi and merely allowed the lance might be untried, so the lance itself matters little to him.

facts.text: Warwick's mithril chain shirt, which Dunk says could help against the dragon (see thread_9).

classification.support_basis: Magical armor would offer some protection in a fight with the dragon, but no specific advantage against it is established.
classification.action_basis: Dunk has a plan to get it, but its benefit against the dragon is only generic protection.
classification.opening_basis: Saying armor could help against the dragon only explains why it would be useful; no enabling circumstance is added.

facts.text: What has become of the shipments to Brandonsford? Bentley's restocking shipment is a week overdue, and others say nothing has come into town for months.

classification.grounding_justification: Several townsfolk independently reported shipments not arriving, and this Session the narration again notes the shipments still haven't come in.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden cause behind a town-wide supply failure lasting months, possibly tied to other troubles.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Explaining why the town has been cut off would change the party's understanding of Brandonsford's troubles.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supports questioning townsfolk and following the supply route out of town.

facts.text: Drop Dead Ned offers himself and his killer wasp for hire at 100 gold for the week, doing anything as long as he gets to kill people, and gives back 5 gold for each person he is allowed to kill; Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.

classification.support_basis: A hired killer with a killer wasp could add fighting strength against the black dragon, but his stated terms centre on killing people, so his value against a dragon is doubtful and the price is steep.
classification.action_basis: Ned explicitly offered his services on stated terms (100 gold a week) to Dr. Uriah, who is considering it; hiring him adds a combatant with a fast-killing wasp.
classification.opening_basis: Ned's standing offer of paid service lets the party add a killer and his killer wasp to its strength by paying 100 gold a week.

facts.text: Get Farmer Gill's mule Shamus, which Gill offers for 100 gold.
Asked whether Dunk could trade work for Shamus, Farmer Gill named killing the dragon as the big work needed.
facts.uncertain_reason: Gill named the work in reply to Dunk's question but never explicitly agreed to trade Shamus for it.

classification.support_basis: Killing the dragon could let Dunk get Shamus without paying 100 gold, though Gill's acceptance of the trade is not confirmed.
classification.action_basis: Gill answered Dunk's question about trading work by naming the dragon kill, an implied but unconfirmed exchange.
classification.opening_basis: Gill wants the dragon killed; doing that work could substitute for the 100 gold price, an alternative route rather than paying the want's own price.

facts.text: Farmer Gill says he will lower his price for Shamus only once his sons come back, since without them or the mule he can't get any work done.

classification.scope_basis: Gill ties the lower price to his sons' return, a lasting condition that holds until they come back, not just during the drinking scene.

facts.text: Help Quinn get back at Bentley, whom Quinn blames for his ale vanishing every night, and collect Quinn's 100 gold.
facts.ended_how: achieved: the thief was caught and proved to be Naggeneen, not Bentley, and Quinn paid Sir Phidipaldi, Trout and Dr. Uriah 33 gold each

facts.text: Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn plan to stage a fake shipment: Quinn supplies bottles filled with water while Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale, to see who comes for the stock at night.
facts.ended_how: obsolete: the thief was caught in the basement with marbles and ink before the decoy shipment was needed

classification.support_basis: A conspicuous decoy delivery could draw out whoever empties Quinn's bar overnight, though it is untested whether the culprit will take the bait.
classification.action_basis: Quinn proposed the staged shipment and Sir Phidipaldi agreed, with Quinn to supply the bottles.
classification.opening_basis: Quinn will supply bottles for a showy decoy delivery; the bait adds a way to catch the nightly taker in the act rather than just accusing Bentley.

facts.text: Who or what empties Quinn's bar every night?
facts.ended_how: answered: the Clurichen Naggeneen was caught taking the alcohol

classification.grounding_justification: Quinn describes a strange recurring pattern of a full bar gone by morning with glasses emptied or knocked over, and only suspects Bentley without proof.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: The answer would reveal a hidden nightly culprit and their motive, not just a simple fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Identifying the culprit would explain an odd mystery and confirm or overturn Quinn's accusation of Bentley.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: It supports a stakeout, the planned decoy shipment and questioning townsfolk.

facts.text: Under the Halfling Corps terms, Trout and the party owe Squints second pick of the first treasure, after the elite members pick first; until then Squints funds himself and buys his own gear.

classification.stake_basis: Squints agreed to fund himself and take Trout's orders in exchange for this share, his only stated pay for joining.

facts.text: Squints, a halfling with a sling and dagger and a more experienced fighter than Trout, serves in the Halfling Corps taking orders directly from Trout; the party privately treats him as expendable.

classification.support_basis: An experienced fighter and scout willing to take risky orders adds a small advantage on the trip to the Barrow for Brandon's sword.

facts.text: Brother Dirk, the monk Father William sent to get Brandon's sword and kill the dragon, has been told by Trout to report to Squints in the Halfling Corps, though Dirk had said he might just head home.
facts.uncertain_reason: Dirk spoke of heading home and never clearly agreed to stay with the party.

classification.support_basis: Dirk was on his way to the Barrow for the sword himself and adds another companion for that trip, but whether he stays is unclear.

facts.resource_subject: Brother Dirk placed under Squints in the Halfling Corps

facts.text: Dunk wants to get the glowing magical mithril chain shirt from Warwick the smith's shop.
Ingrid's sleeping potion, which Dunk plans to help her give Warwick, could keep Warwick asleep while Dunk gets into the shop for the shirt.

classification.support_basis: A sleeping Warwick would let Dunk enter the shop and take the shirt without being caught; the potion is not yet made.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to make the sleeping potion and Dunk proposed to help her get in and give it to Warwick, and he says he has a plan to get the shirt.
classification.opening_basis: A potion that sedates the shop's sleeping owner removes the risk of him waking during entry, an advantage beyond simply taking the shirt.

facts.resource_subject: The sleeping potion and its faun-wine ingredient

facts.text: Warwick sleeps in a second-story bedroom of his shop-home whose window is left cracked open at night, offering a way inside.

classification.support_basis: The open window gives a route into the closed shop where the shirt is kept, though it opens into the room where Warwick sleeps.
classification.action_basis: Dunk observed the window cracked open; climbing in is a physical option requiring no one's cooperation.
classification.opening_basis: An open upper window provides entry to the locked, closed shop, bypassing the door.

facts.text: What magic does Warwick's glowing mithril chain shirt hold?

classification.grounding_justification: The shirt is described as glowing and clearly magical but nobody raises what it does.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: Identifying an item's property is a simple fact.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mainly instrumental information about an item.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Likely settled by examining the item or a lookup.

facts.text: Ingrid is working on a sleeping potion using the faun wine Dunk brought. Dunk plans to help her into Warwick's house and give it to Warwick so he sleeps through the night, which would get Dunk inside with the smith asleep.

classification.support_basis: A sleeping Warwick and Ingrid's help getting in would let Dunk reach the mithril shirt, but the potion is unmade and the faun wine was heavily diluted.
classification.action_basis: Ingrid agreed to work on the potion after receiving the faun wine, and Dunk plans to meet her tonight to carry out the plan.
classification.opening_basis: Ingrid is brewing a sleeping potion and has night access to Warwick's window. Dosing Warwick and entering with her would get Dunk past the sleeping owner into the house, beyond simply wanting the shirt.

facts.resource_subject: The sleeping potion and its faun-wine ingredient

facts.text: Dunk owes Ingrid his help getting her into Warwick's house and giving Warwick the sleeping potion once she has made it, so she can watch him all night.

classification.stake_basis: Ingrid fears Warwick waking and is making the potion on Dunk's proposal that he would help her get in to watch Warwick safely.

facts.text: Ingrid climbs to Warwick's window every night in secret and most fears he will learn she watches him. Dunk has hinted he might not keep her secret, which gives him leverage over her.

classification.support_basis: Knowing her secret and her fear of exposure could press Ingrid to keep cooperating with the plan to get into Warwick's house.

facts.resource_subject: Ingrid's secret nightly visits to Warwick's window

facts.text: Will the sleeping potion work when made with Dunk's heavily diluted faun wine?

classification.grounding_justification: Dunk deliberately cut the key ingredient to about 20% faun wine before handing it over, which plainly raises whether the potion can work.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: A bounded property of the potion that testing would settle.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Settled by asking Ingrid or trying the potion.

facts.text: Can Ingrid really make her potions herself, as she says, or is Father William right that she can't?

classification.grounding_justification: Father William's claim and Ingrid's denial directly contradict each other.
classification.investigative_depth_justification: It could reveal whether Vivian or her coven supplies the potions, but it is largely a single fact about her ability.
classification.narrative_payoff_justification: Mildly interesting, since it bears on Ingrid's ties to the witch, but mainly practical.
classification.investigative_potential_justification: Watching her work or asking Vivian could settle it.

facts.text: The fauns of the Faun Grove trade their wine for sentimental items, such as a love letter or a pixie's treasure, if more faun wine is needed for the potion.

classification.support_basis: It is a further source of the potion's key ingredient if the diluted wine falls short; it is not yet known to be needed.
classification.action_basis: The fauns already traded Dunk a flask of wine for a rabbit's foot and said they trade for sentimental items.

facts.text: Father William says the black dragon can't be killed without the magic sword buried with Brandon in Brandon's Barrow Mound; the party could retrieve it from the Barrow.

facts.text: A man-eating giant lives in a huge stone cottage in the woods along the party's route north; he captured Brother Dirk to cook in a stew and may seize travelers who pass.

classification.negative_outcome_clarity_justification: Dirk says the giant meant to eat him in a stew, a specific identifiable harm: being captured and eaten.
classification.outcome_severity_justification: Being captured and eaten means death for whoever is taken.
classification.evidentiary_strength_justification: The party saw the giant and its captive directly, and Dirk testified to its intent.
classification.evidence_of_progression_justification: The giant had already captured a traveler heading to the Barrow and chased the party, but nothing shows he is actively hunting them now.
classification.preventability_justification: The giant is slow and was easily outrun, and the party knows where his cottage is and can avoid it.
